newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu pressing Egypt to free suspected spy.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu pressing Egypt to free suspected spy.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday he was pressing Egypt to release a suspected Israeli spy detained last month.

"I personally am working, at the most senior levels in Egypt, to bring about the release of Azam Azam," Netanyahu told relatives of the Israeli Druze Arab during a meeting in the prime minister's office.
"He is innocent. He has to be returned to Israel and we are working so that he will be handed back as soon as possible," Netanyahu said in broadcast remarks. "He will be here very soon."
Azam, 35, chief mechanic at an Israeli-owned textile factory in Egypt, was arrested in Cairo last month by security authorities along with Egyptian Emadeddin Abdel Hamid.
Egyptian security sources have said Abdel Hamid has confessed to spying for Israel and receiving espionage equipment from Azam, who has been detained in Egypt on the same charges.
Azam and two Israeli women, who are not in Egypt, are charged with recruiting Abdel Hamid to spy for Israel's intelligence service Mossad.
The official charge sheet detailing accusations against the two men and two women is ready and will be announced any time, an Egyptian public prosecution source said on Wednesday.
Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab country to sign a peace treaty with Israel but ties have cooled sharply since the right-wing Netanyahu took office in June.
